summary: PJM files tariff revisions under section 205 on November 16, 2026, in a new docket, ER27-531-000. It proposes a 12-month Fast Energization Process that studies generators and large loads together, three new transmission services for large and co-located loads, a 50 MW limit on netting behind-the-meter generation, and a refiled version of its August 17 co-location compliance changes.
ask: Accept the revisions, mostly effective March 16, 2027 with Fast Energization on an indefinite date; allow 60 days for comments, rule within 120 days, and close the section 206 case.

points.point: Generator interconnection requests and large-load service requests would be studied together in one 12-month process.
points.quote: which will study together New Service Requests, including Generation Interconnection Requests, and requests from Eligible Customers seeking transmission service on behalf of Eligible Load

points.point: PJM says the new process should take half the time of today's cycle process.
points.quote: The process will take half the time of the Cycle process.

points.point: The first Fast Energization submission window would not open until late November 2027.
points.quote: the Submission Window for the first Cycle under the Fast Energization Process would open in late November 2027

points.point: Customers with retail behind-the-meter generation could net no more than 50 MW of it from their load, as the co-location order directed.
points.quote: PJM is proposing revisions to Part III, section 34.2 and Schedule 8 of the RAA to implement the 50 MW netting limit.

points.point: Interim NITS would let large and co-located loads use spare capacity on an interruptible basis.
points.quote: Interim NITS is a transmission service that allows Eligible Customers serving Eligible Load or Large Load to utilize head room on the system as-available on an interruptible basis

points.point: PJM's Fast Energization Process studies transmission service and generator interconnection requests together to serve electrically proximate load and generation.
points.quote: to optimize the Transmission System and yield efficiencies for electrically proximate load and generation

points.point: PJM's own table maps the order's generator-interconnection concern to a single cycle that studies generation and load together.
points.quote: Generation and load studied together in one Cycle; IRRs optimized for the whole cohort; interim deliverability schedules

points.point: Customers asking for service for a Large Load must sign a Transmission Owner Cost Recovery Agreement to enter the process, and developers post readiness deposits in full.
points.quote: The Fast Energization Process requires Eligible Customers seeking service on behalf of Large Loads to enter into a Transmission Owner Cost Recovery Agreement as a condition of entering the process

points.point: PJM would post upgrade drivers and capital costs in one searchable place on its website.
points.quote: PJM will post the required system topology, the drivers of the need for the IRRs, and their capital costs on pjm.com in a single, accessible, and searchable location

points.point: A customer taking the firm contract demand service would be curtailed on the same footing as network and firm point-to-point service.
points.quote: FCD Transmission Service will be treated as equivalent to NITS and Firm Point-to-Point Transmission Services for purposes of Curtailment.

throughLine.text: Filed under section 205 to answer the E-7 show cause order for PJM. It also refiles PJM's E-2 co-location compliance changes, replacing the August 17 filing PJM withdrew the same day.
